title: The Fiat Off-Ramp
_comment: The EXIT — turning crypto back into fiat, and the mirror of the on-ramp (ON). NOT live-captured: code-traced from MetaMask's Sell / ramp aggregator (on-ramp.api.cx.metamask.io, same API family as Buy) and the MoonPay/Coinbase sell providers, with the bank-payout + AML legs inferred (they sit behind the provider). Two things make the off-ramp WORSE than the on-ramp. First, you must hand over a BANK ACCOUNT to RECEIVE the wire — full legal identity plus a payout destination. Second, and unique to the exit: you SIGN and broadcast an on-chain transaction sending your crypto to the provider, which permanently and PUBLICLY links that address to your KYC'd identity — anyone reading the chain can tie the two together forever. And because the crypto leaves your custody BEFORE the fiat arrives, the provider can freeze the payout (an AML flag, a sanctions hit, a bad region) after you have already given up the coins. The zero-option question is even starker than the on-ramp: there is essentially no private fiat exit through these rails — the only 'zero option' is to spend crypto directly or sell peer-to-peer for cash, both thin. Provenance: code/inferred, no purchase or KYC or payment ever entered — this flow needs a live capture to confirm (it is on the Evidence validation queue).

steps.name: MetaMask sell · geolocation
steps.purpose: Geolocate you the moment Sell opens, to decide your region
steps.returns: your region — which gates which providers can pay you out
steps.failure_note: no region → no off-ramp providers offered

worst_lie.note: the region it assigns decides who is allowed to buy your crypto and wire you fiat

provenance.ref: MetaMask Sell uses the same ramp aggregator as Buy (on-ramp.api.cx.metamask.io/geolocation, observed on the Buy capture); the Sell path itself was NOT captured

steps.name: MetaMask sell · region-gated providers + quote
steps.purpose: Return the sell providers, payout methods, and a quote allowed in your jurisdiction
steps.returns: the list of providers permitted to pay you out, and how much fiat you'd get
steps.failure_note: empty list in an unsupported region → you cannot cash out at all

worst_lie.note: your jurisdiction decides who can pay you; the quote also frames what you accept

provenance.ref: mirrors the Buy region/provider endpoint for the sell direction; exact sell path not captured

steps.notes: The amount you're cashing out is part of the request — the provider list is jurisdiction-gated exactly like the on-ramp.

steps.name: MoonPay · KYC + bank for payout
steps.purpose: The chosen provider runs full KYC and takes a BANK ACCOUNT to wire the fiat to
steps.returns: clearance to sell — once it has your legal identity AND a payout bank account
steps.failure_note: fail KYC, or an unsupported bank/region → no payout

worst_lie.note: the provider holds your identity, your bank link, and the on/off switch on your exit from crypto

provenance.ref: api.moonpay.com (real host, seen on the Buy side); the sell KYC + bank collection sits behind the provider and was NOT entered

steps.notes: The identity + bank SINK. Worse than the on-ramp: the on-ramp took a card to CHARGE you; the off-ramp takes a bank account to PAY you — a durable financial link, plus tax reporting.

steps.name: MoonPay · deposit address
steps.purpose: The provider returns the address you must send your crypto to
steps.returns: the provider's deposit address — now tied to your KYC record

worst_lie.note: a swapped deposit address sends your crypto to an attacker; you have no recourse

provenance.ref: standard sell flow: the provider issues a per-order deposit address; not captured

steps.notes: The moment your address is bound to your legal identity in the provider's records — before anything is even sent.

steps.name: Send crypto to the provider · RPC broadcast
steps.purpose: You sign and broadcast an on-chain tx moving your crypto to the provider's address
steps.returns: a public, permanent on-chain record linking your address to the provider (and your KYC)
steps.failure_note: the RPC can withhold your broadcast

worst_lie.note: the broadcast node can drop or delay the tx; your crypto is committed to the provider once it lands

provenance.ref: standard eth_sendRawTransaction via the default MetaMask RPC (Infura); identical to the send leg on every other map

steps.notes: UNIQUE to the off-ramp: unlike the on-ramp (no signing, crypto arrives to you), here you SIGN a public tx. That transaction ties this address to your KYC'd identity forever, readable by anyone.

steps.name: Block builder · inclusion
steps.purpose: A builder includes your send-to-provider tx in a block
steps.returns: your exit tx, public in a block

provenance.ref: every mainnet tx passes a builder/relay; inclusion inferred from protocol, not a wallet call

steps.name: MoonPay · AML screen + bank wire
steps.purpose: The provider screens the payout, then wires fiat to your bank — after it already holds your crypto
steps.returns: fiat in your bank — or a frozen payout
steps.failure_note: an AML/sanctions flag can freeze the payout after you've sent the crypto

worst_lie.note: the crypto left your custody BEFORE the fiat arrives; the provider can hold or claw the payout

provenance.ref: AML screening + bank wire + tax reporting sit behind the provider and the banking rails; not observable from the client

steps.notes: The asymmetry that defines the off-ramp: you give up custody first, the fiat comes second, and a screen sits in between. Tax authorities are reported to here too.
